ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$21.56 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (the metered excess of the unexcused loop above the 13.86 km / 20.5 min quote); do not refund the S$0.11 metered waiting time; note the driver's RD-1 breach and his unsupported "short stop" claim in his file, but no account flag (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0).
ruling.reasoning: Service is RydeTAXI, metered (fare.pricing = metered; total 39.18 = 3.90 + 26.31 + 7.39 + 0.11 + 1.47), so detour distance flows straight into the fare (policy §0 / RD-2). Recorded meter distance 18.66 km vs quoted route 13.86 km = 4.80 km of extra driving, and the GPS track (21:34 pickup → 22:02:50 drop-off) follows the quoted polyline only while heading east on the PIE corridor (21:35–21:38); at 21:38:30–21:39:30 it leaves that corridor and doubles back west (1.32787,103.86811 → 1.32900,103.86514 → 1.32807,103.86296) — first off-route loop; then at 21:40–21:48 it drives a further anomalous zig-zag along the AYE corridor (21:42 1.32284,103.87025; 21:44:30 1.31044,103.87258; 21:46:30 1.31144,103.86221; 21:48:00 1.31547,103.85636) — second, longer loop of roughly 1.9 km. Vehicles cannot be stationary on the AYE/PIE, so the "band 5 / 0–9 km/h stop" links the incident-json includes are artefacts; every matched inland leg of the quoted route is free-flow (band 5), and there is no incident record, so nothing excuses either loop (RD-4, RD-1). The chat is decisive: 21:35:40 driver: "Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty."; 21:36:15 rider: "Sure, no problem." The rider named no place, the driver chose it (RD-3(b)), and the consent covers a brief stop, not a looping route — the words' scope is a short stop, so neither loop is covered (RD-5, scope_other). The record also shows no stop at all: the car is moving 36–45 km/h at the start and end of both loops (21:38:30 37.8; 21:39:30 36.9; 21:48:00 44.8; 21:48:30 36.9), so no petrol was taken; the driver's statement ("rider agreed to a short stop so a small change of route was fine") is both unevidenced (G11) and contradicted by the data. Both segments count. Refund per RD-2: 4.80 km extra × unit rate (fare.distance_fare 26.31 ÷ fare.distance_km 18.66 = 1.41 $/km) = 6.77, plus the proportional metered time component 4.80 × (7.39 ÷ 28.42 = 0.26 $/min) = 1.25 → 8.02 in raw units; the record's own charge above the 13.86 km/20.5 min quote is 26.31 + 7.39 − 12.14 = 21.56 (the fare is metered whole-trip, so every metre and second of the loop is charged), and that is the actual excess the rider paid, so 21.56 is refunded as a Ryde voucher (NS-7). Scope of refund: only the extra mileage/time; the S$0.11 metered waiting time is not refunded (RD-3(c) — RydeTAXI keeps metered waiting units), and there is no toll/ERP item to review (tolls 0.00, no FARE-2 trigger). No account flag: the driver's route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's repeated-offence condition is not met. Downgraded to 0.72 partly because the loop segments had to be identified from thinned (30 s) sampling and because the size of the refund follows the fare record's own excess rather than one official Ryde formula (G5).

segment_findings.reason: Consent at 21:36:15 was to a short petrol stop only ('Sure, no problem' to the driver's 21:35:40 'pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute'); the rider named no place and the record shows no stop. The ~1.1 km westward doubling-back loop (GPS 21:38:30–21:39:30: 1.32787,103.86811 → 1.32900,103.86514 → 1.32807,103.86296 → 1.32805,103.86795) began after the consent message and leads nowhere; unexcused — RD-3(b) / RD-5 scope = scope_other, RD-1 violation, refund under RD-2.

The larger ~1.9 km east-then-south loop off both the quoted route and the PIE/AYE corridor (GPS 21:40–21:48: 1.32284,103.87025 → 1.31044,103.87258 → 1.31144,103.86221 → 1.31547,103.85636), which is not on the quoted polyline and ends at a starting point roughly the distance of a fuel garage circuit; no rider message asked for it and no stop occurred (36–45 km/h throughout), i.e. the driver's own deviation. Matched inland legs are LTA band 5 (free-flow) so RD-4 gives no reasonable cause; counts under RD-1, refunded under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim that a 'small change of route' was fine because the rider agreed to a short stop is contradicted by the chat (the rider agreed only to a one-minute petrol stop) and by the GPS: no stop exists in the trace (car moving 36–45 km/h at the start/end of both loops), and the loops of ~1.1 km and ~1.9 km were driven without any stop and with no incident or congestion to justify them (all matched legs band 5).

The rider's 'meter was higher than the estimate' is accepted on the mileage ground (18.66 m vs 13.86 km quoted), but this is not a non-metered fixed-quote overcharge; the fare is metered, so recovery is limited to the unexcused detour mileage and its proportional time, per RD-2.
